paragraphs: Rav Chana bar Chanilai was associated with Rav Chisda. He performed many acts of charity: there were sixty bakings in his house by day and by night; he gave to whoever needed, never took his hand from his purse, and whoever entered hungry left satisfied, etc. His house was destroyed, and Ulla and Rav Chisda said, “It is enough for the servant to be like his master”: HaRoeh, Berakhot 58b. Another version has Rav Chanan bar Tuvi. Rav Huna decreed a fast; R. Chana bar Chanilai entered his presence: Megillah 27a, near the end. Rav Huna carried a spade on his shoulder; R. Chana bar Chanilai came and wished to take it from him, but Rav Huna did not wish it: there, 28a. He came before Rav Huna, and “he is a great man”: Beitzah 40a. He objects to what Rav Chisda said: Beitzah 21a.
